findings.text: The legacy 'command:name' event now fires on the parent instead of the command. Existing code that does `cmd.on('command:name', ...)` on the command itself, which worked before, never fires. The emit also happens only when `this.parent` is set, so a root program with an action handler never emits at all.

The new `else if (parent.listenerCount(commandEvent))` branch runs for a subcommand with no action handler. It emits and skips the `operands.length` handling below it, which dispatches to the '*' command, emits 'command:*', or reports an unknown command. Example: the parent has `.on('command:sub', ...)` and `sub` has its own subcommands, and the user runs `prog sub bogus`. The unknown-command error and help are swallowed.
